title: Improve error messages for incompatible quantization profiles (Console + API remediation hints)
author: Chloe Martin
description:
Context: As we onboard design partners to route-level quantization profiles, we’re seeing repeated confusion when enabling a profile fails due to compatibility checks (GPU SKU class mismatch, max context constraints, deployment tier restrictions, or profile state=deprecated/blocked). Today the API returns a generic 400/409 with an internal-ish reason string, and Console collapses it to “Incompatible profile” with no next steps. This PR improves the user-facing error payloads for route quantization enablement and surfaces concrete remediation hints in Console and SDK-facing API responses. Goals: (1) make the failure reason unambiguous, (2) provide suggested next steps (pick a compatible profile, lower max_context, change region/tier, or leave default), (3) keep determinism and safety semantics unchanged (still safe-fallback at runtime; this is purely about configuration-time feedback), and (4) ensure errors are stable/typed so Console can render consistent UX.

What changed (high level): Added a typed incompatibility error model returned from the control-plane quantization settings endpoints; mapped policy-engine compatibility failures to a small set of public error codes; included structured ‘remediation’ hints (human-readable + machine fields) and ‘details’ for advanced users; updated Console backend to pass through the structured payload; updated Console UI copy to show a summary + expandable details and “Suggested fixes” (e.g., change region, pick a different profile version, reduce max_context, or disable). Also added better error messages when the profile ref resolves to a profile that is (a) deprecated, (b) blocked by quality guardrails, or (c) not published to the tenant’s allowed catalog.

API shape (before -> after): Before: 400 {"error":"incompatible quantization profile"}. After: 409 QUANT_PROFILE_INCOMPATIBLE with payload fields: error_code, message, incompatibility_reasons[], remediation_suggestions[], and request_context (route_id, model_id, resolved_profile_id, region, deployment_tier, gpu_class, max_context). Notes: request_context is redacted to non-sensitive identifiers only (no prompt content, no tenant secrets). We keep backwards compatibility by still including the legacy ‘error’ string at top level for one release cycle.

Examples:
- GPU mismatch: message="Profile requires GPU_CLASS=A100_OR_EQUIV; route is running on L4"; remediation="Select a profile compatible with L4, or move the route to a tier/region backed by A100.".
- Context cap: message="Profile validated up to max_context=8192; route configured for 16384"; remediation="Lower route max_context to <=8192 or choose a profile version that supports 16384.".
- Guardrail blocked: message="Profile v3 blocked due to quality regression (policy: Q-REG-INT8-2025-03-17)"; remediation="Select a different profile version or use default (baseline) until a new version is published.".

Implementation notes: The policy engine already computes compatibility; we now convert internal reasons into stable public enums (GPU_CLASS_MISMATCH, MAX_CONTEXT_EXCEEDED, DEPLOYMENT_TIER_UNSUPPORTED, REGION_UNPUBLISHED, PROFILE_DEPRECATED, PROFILE_BLOCKED, MODEL_VARIANT_MISMATCH). Console consumes the structured list and renders a consistent UX. We also updated tracing/logging to attach error_code + primary_reason for debugging. No runtime behavior changes.

Testing: Added unit tests for reason mapping, golden tests for API error payloads, and an integration test that exercises Console backend -> control plane error propagation. Manually verified in staging by attempting to enable an A100-only INT8 profile on an L4-backed hosted route and by setting max_context above supported cap.

Rollout: Safe to merge; error payloads are additive. Console uses the new structured fields when present, otherwise falls back to the legacy string. We can backport if needed for beta partners reporting confusion.

Screenshots: Console modal now shows: “This profile can’t be enabled for this route” + ‘Why?’ list + ‘Suggested fixes’ list with links to ‘View compatible profiles’ and ‘Update route settings’. (See internal screenshot link in review thread.)
commits: control-plane: add QuantProfileCompatibilityError + public reason codes
policy-engine: map internal incompat reasons to stable public enums
api: include remediation_suggestions and request_context in 409 responses
console: render suggested fixes + details accordion; update copy
tests: golden payload tests + integration coverage for route enablement
conversation: Ethan Park (review): Love the direction. Can we standardize on 409 for incompatibility vs 400? Also please confirm legacy clients still see a useful message.

Chloe Martin (author): Yep—switched to 409 for QUANT_PROFILE_INCOMPATIBLE; kept legacy `error` string and `message` field. Added a golden test to ensure the legacy `error` remains present for one release cycle.
Naomi Feldman (review): Request_context: ensure we are not leaking tenant identifiers in ways that violate audit/export policies. Route IDs are ok; tenant_id should not be included.
Chloe Martin (author): Agreed—removed tenant_id from request_context. Route_id is already visible in Console and audit logs. Added a redaction test to prevent regressions.
Dylan Brooks (review): Console UX: can we include a link to “View compatible profiles” and a copy tweak to avoid sounding like a hard failure (since runtime falls back)?

Chloe Martin (author): Added link to the profile picker filtered by model_id + region. Copy updated to: “This selection can’t be applied to this route configuration. Requests will continue using the default profile.”
Ravi Menon (review): For MAX_CONTEXT_EXCEEDED, remediation should mention lowering max_context OR choosing a profile validated for that length, but not imply we will auto-truncate.
Chloe Martin (author): Updated suggestion text. Also added explicit note in details: “No automatic truncation performed by this setting.”
Jada Williams (review): Please ensure we emit an audit event for failed attempts? At least log an event with actor + route + error_code for compliance investigations.

Chloe Martin (author): We don’t want to create audit noise for failed attempts in v1, but I added a structured security log event (not audit-log exported) with actor_id hash + route_id + error_code. Confirmed with Naomi this is acceptable for now.
Ethan Park (review): One more: region unpublished vs region unsupported. The reason codes should be distinct and stable.
Chloe Martin (author): Split into REGION_UNPUBLISHED (profile not available in region) vs DEPLOYMENT_TIER_UNSUPPORTED (tier/gpu class). Added tests + docs comments in mapping file.
Dylan Brooks (review): Approved after latest changes. Thanks for adding the remediation list; this will help beta partners a lot.
release_notes: Console/API: When enabling a quantization profile fails due to incompatibility, responses now include typed error codes with clear reasons and suggested remediation steps (e.g., pick a compatible profile, adjust region/tier, or lower max_context).
